issues.description: The template's ArrayHelpers defines a method named appendElement(T[] array, T element) but Stock.addToStockIngredients calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). This name/signature mismatch causes the template to not compile and prevents students from using the helper as suggested in the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the helper method name consistent. Either rename the method in the template's ArrayHelpers from appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...), or update Stock.addToStockIngredients to call appendElement(...). Prefer matching the solution and Stock usage by implementing addElementToArray in ArrayHelpers so students can compile and follow the provided examples.

issues.description: The helper method used to append elements to arrays has inconsistent identifiers across the repositories: the template ArrayHelpers defines appendElement(...) while the template Stock class calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). The solution repository consistently uses addElementToArray(...). This mismatch will confuse students and cause compilation errors because the method referenced by Stock does not exist in the template ArrayHelpers implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Rename the template ArrayHelpers.appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) (matching the solution) or change Stock.addToStockIngredients to call appendElement(...). Prefer renaming appendElement to addElementToArray so the template matches the solution and all references (Stock.java) compile and are conceptually consistent.
